title: 2026-09-10-deployment-pathways-and-data-control-probe-with-boreal-insurance
summary: Initial residency and compliance discovery for LLM features. Boreal is evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private for PII-sensitive claims classification and policy assistant. Key constraints: EU data residency for EU customers, HIPAA overlap for health-related claims, strict audit logs (legal-hold), KMS control, and limited log retention. Next steps: send compliance pack, pricing for Dedicated, run a short benchmark in VPC/private staging.
topics: audit logs and legal hold workflow

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-09-10 11:00 AM BST / 06:00 PT
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Samir P., Leah G., Marco R. (Redwood); Alex R., Priya M., Evan Z., Marta K. (Boreal)

Auto-generated summary: Boreal wants clarity on how Redwood will keep EU customer data within EU, options for keeping keys customer-controlled, and what logs Redwood keeps in the control plane. They are comfortable with cloud providers but need strong auditability and legal-hold capabilities.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir, AE at Redwood, and Leah and Marco from our team are with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:04] Alex Raines: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to get into this.
[00:06] Priya Malhotra: Hi. We wanted to make sure we covered GDPR boundaries and a couple of HIPAA-ish questions because we process some wellness-related claims in EMEA.
[00:12] Leah Gomez: Totally. We'll try to map options end-to-end — hosted, dedicated, private — and call out where keys/logs live and what evidence we can provide. Quick note: there may be small transcription noise, so shout if something's off.
[00:22] Evan Zhou: Quick context: we have an existing inference pipeline on AWS, multi-account, currently using customer-managed KMS. We don't want plaintext PII to leave the EU control plane.
[00:31] Marco Ruiz: Got it. When you say "leave the EU control plane" do you mean both inference data and logs?
[00:36] Evan Zhou: Yes. Model inputs for EU customers must remain in EU, and logs/audit traces for those requests should be stored in EU, with access limited to our security team.
[00:44] Priya Malhotra: And for legal hold — if a regulator asks us to preserve chat transcripts for x days — we need a chain of custody and the ability to put holds across exports.
[00:52] Samir Patel: Great. High level: Hosted API is fastest but control plane and some audit metadata reside in Redwood's control plane regions — we can region-lock logs to EU regions for you but keys are Redwood-managed by default. Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and can be deployed in cloud regions of your choice with stronger tenancy and can offer customer-managed keys. Private (VPC/self-managed) gives you full control of the control plane, keystore in your KMS, and we can ship a package for air-gapped setups.
[01:20] Alex Raines: So, if we choose Dedicated, can we keep the keystore in our KMS? Or does Redwood require key escrow?
[01:26] Leah Gomez: For Dedicated we support KMS integration. You can bring your own keys (BYOK) and we support wrapping/sealing. For Private we can leave all control-plane artifacts in your VPC and never pull keys into Redwood-managed KMS. There is a small operational delta: with Private you manage upgrades; with Dedicated we handle runtime but KMS calls can be proxied through a customer KMS in the same region.
[01:45] Marta Kovac: When you say "proxy KMS calls" — is that an egress? We need assurance that key materials do not transit outside region boundaries.
[01:51] Leah Gomez: The proxy makes API calls to your KMS endpoint in-region; keys never leave the KMS. We provide an audit verb log showing key usage events — those logs can be pushed to your logging bucket in the same region.
[02:05] Priya Malhotra: What about runtime caches, like KV cache or prefix caches? If an inference request references past context, where is that KV stored and for how long?
[02:13] Leah Gomez: Good question. By default for Hosted we keep ephemeral KV in memory per shard and it's not persisted beyond the session. For Dedicated/Private we can configure cache eviction and persistence policies; for strict compliance you'd likely want no cross-tenant persistence and short TTLs.
[02:29] Evan Zhou: Are there logs of requests (metadata like IP, timestamps, token counts) that Redwood keeps in the control plane? We need to control retention.
[02:35] Samir Patel: Yes, we capture tracing metadata for performance and billing. We can offer log minimization: redact IPs, minimize request/response logging for EU-scoped tenants, and support region-local retention policies.
[02:47] Alex Raines: Does that include the control-plane audit trail for administrative actions? We have strict requirements to produce admin action logs for SOC2 and regulator audits.
[02:55] Marco Ruiz: Admin audit logs are separate and can be integrated into your SIEM. We keep immutable audit trails for role changes, key rotation events, model rollouts. For Dedicated/Private we can push those into your S3 buckets or Splunk instance in-region.
[03:08] Priya Malhotra: What about legal hold? If legal team asks to freeze all logs/requests for a subject, can we place a hold that prevents deletion across backups?
[03:16] Leah Gomez: We have a legal-hold workflow in the console — you can flag entities and we create immutable snapshots and prevent TTL-based deletion. For Hosted it's a managed capability; for Dedicated/Private we give hooks so your ops team can enforce holds within your infrastructure.
[03:29] Priya Malhotra: Okay. Need to see that in writing — retention windows, deletion proofs, WORM-like storage.
[03:35] Samir Patel: Absolutely. We'll include the retention matrix and proof artifacts in the pack.
[03:39] [04:00] Alex Raines: Another operational question — does Redwood ever index or store model outputs for training or internal evaluation? We're strict about not allowing our customer data into vendor training corpora.
[04:08] Samir Patel: Redwood does not use customer data for model training by default. We have an opt-in feedback loop for improvement but for enterprise accounts we can disable all telemetry feeding into model training and provide attestations.
[04:21] Evan Zhou: Good. How granular is RBAC? We need role-separated access: platform engineers vs business analysts vs security — especially around viewing redacted transcripts vs full content.
[04:30] Marco Ruiz: We expose token-level permissions. You can set routes where only certain roles can request full-text dumps; others receive redacted or metadata-only results. SAML/SCIM provisioning is supported for automating role assignment.
[04:44] Marta Kovac: Are redactions automatic or manual? We need to ensure PII is masked before any non-sec team sees it.
[04:49] Leah Gomez: We support both. You can configure automated redaction rules (regex and entity-based) at ingest and also require manual review gates. For Dedicated we can add an enforced pre-view redaction step.
[05:02] Priya Malhotra: For EU residency, can we guarantee that logs and model inputs never traverse outside monitored network paths? E.g., no control-plane replication to US regions?
[05:10] Samir Patel: For Dedicated/Private you can request region-locking: control plane artifacts for EU tenants remain in EU and we suppress cross-region replication. For Hosted we have region-tiered options but by default some control-plane analytics aggregate in multi-region. We can provide a contract clause for data locality for your deal.
[05:28] Alex Raines: What about key escrow — we've seen vendors ask to escrow keys in case of disaster recovery. We're not comfortable with that unless there's a strict KMS escrow policy.
[05:36] Leah Gomez: Key escrow is optional and can be structured with HSM-backed escrow and split-key custody with your security team. Many customers avoid escrow and instead run Private/Dedicated with BYOK to remove the need.
[05:48] Evan Zhou: Latency question: if we put KMS in-region and run Dedicated in EU, what's the typical p50/p95 for generation? We need sub-250ms p95 for short prompts (~256 tokens).
[05:58] Marco Ruiz: That depends on model size and instance type. For a 7B-ish model on a dedicated pool, p50 might be ~60–90ms, p95 under 200–250ms for short prompts. We can run a benchmark with your workloads.
[06:12] Alex Raines: Can we benchmark using our sample flows in a private staging environment?
[06:16] Leah Gomez: Yes. We can stand up a Dedicated staging cluster in your cloud account (or a Private staging with a trial package) and run the test harness. Leah will follow up with the plan.
[06:25] Priya Malhotra: Audit evidence — what paperwork can you produce for regulators? SOC2, ISO27001, encryption attestation, KMS usage logs, redaction proofs?
[06:33] Samir Patel: We'll send SOC2 Type II, ISO certs, and an evidence bundle. For KMS usage we can provide signed logs and key usage attestations; for redaction proofs we can provide before/after samples with hashing to prove content changed.
[06:47] Marta Kovac: If we go Hosted but lock EU tenants, who has admin access to control-plane consoles in your ops team? We need a whitelist and audited break-glass procedures.
[06:57] Marco Ruiz: For Hosted we operate the control plane; access is limited to a small ops team and we have break-glass with two-person approval and full audit logs. We can enter a contractual SLA that any access is logged and a customer notification is sent.
[07:10] Alex Raines: On the legal side, if a regulator subpoenas data and it's in your control plane, what is the flow? We need to ensure we are quickly informed and that data stays in-region if subpoena relates to EU customers.
[07:19] Samir Patel: We have a legal team process: any third-party request goes through our legal and we notify the customer per contract. For region-specific subpoena we commit to defend data residency in the first instance, and coordinate with your counsel. We'll provide the steps in the pack.
[07:33] Priya Malhotra: Two technical gotchas we saw with other vendors: 1) hidden telemetry in URL params or request headers; 2) inadvertent logging of full model responses in tracing. Can Redwood guarantee these are redacted?
[07:43] Leah Gomez: We run sanitization on headers and query params and have a redaction pipeline for traces. We can guarantee that by default certain fields are never stored, and you can extend the sanitizers for your patterns.
[07:56] Evan Zhou: Is there a way to push all logs to our logging account so nothing is stored in Redwood's buckets?
[08:01] Marco Ruiz: With Dedicated we can push all logs to your account/S3 and we retain only ephemeral pointers. With Private nothing leaves your account unless you opt in.
[08:10] Alex Raines: Pricing aside, which path do customers like us typically pick? We are mid-size insurer with regulated EMEA business.
[08:16] Samir Patel: Many in your space start with Dedicated to get isolation and BYOK while offloading operations. Large regulated customers sometimes go Private when they require air-gap or full offline control. Hosted is chosen by teams who prioritize speed and don't need strict residency.
[08:30] Priya Malhotra: Timeline question: we want to pilot in Q4 2026 and decide by end of year. Is that feasible?
[08:36] Leah Gomez: Yes. If you sign for a pilot in early Oct we can provision a Dedicated staging cluster and run benchmarks in 2–3 weeks. Private packaging takes longer (typically 6–10 weeks) because of deployment/testing.
[08:49] Alex Raines: Ok that's helpful. A few follow-ups on encryption: do you support HSM-backed keys and split custody?
[08:56] Leah Gomez: Yes, we integrate with cloud HSMs and can support split custody workflows. We also support bringing an HSM-backed key via your KMS provider.
[09:06] Marta Kovac: Regarding backups: where are old log backups stored and for how long? Can we request periodic proof-of-deletion?
[09:13] Marco Ruiz: Backups for Hosted are in our control-plane storage, with region options; retention configurable per-tenant. We can provide deletion proofs (signed manifests) for Dedicated/Private where you control the buckets.
[09:26] Evan Zhou: Are there any features that only exist in Hosted and not in Private? Like some analytics or automated eval dashboards?
[09:33] Samir Patel: Some SaaS analytics (aggregated usage dashboards) are SaaS-only. But we can provide equivalent telemetry exports and a packaged dashboard for Dedicated/Private. Certain managed features like auto-scaling across regional pools are easier in Hosted.
[09:48] Alex Raines: Quick question on data minimization — if we route a call through Redwood and it triggers a fallback to a smaller cheap model due to capacity, will that fallback model be in a different region? We want no unexpected cross-region processing.
[09:59] Leah Gomez: You can pin model variants and region policies so fallbacks remain in-region only. Smart routing can be configured with strict locality constraints.
[10:09] Priya Malhotra: For audit readiness, can you simulate a regulator request and provide the full chain-of-custody sample?
[10:16] Marco Ruiz: Yes, we can run an evidence simulation as part of the pilot and produce a reproducible package.
[10:21] Samir Patel: Going to summarize: we'll send the compliance pack (SOC2, ISO, HIPAA attestation), detail on KMS/BYOK and escrow options, legal-hold workflow docs, and a Dedicated pricing plan. Leah will send a benchmark plan to run in your staging account. We'll schedule a security-only deep dive on Sept 17 with Priya and Marta. Any objections?
[10:39] Priya Malhotra: No objections, just need the docs and proof artifacts.
[10:43] Alex Raines: Sounds good. Appreciate the thoroughness.
[10:45] Evan Zhou: I'll prepare the sample flows; we'll aim to have them to you by the 14th.
[10:49] Samir Patel: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with an email and shared drive links.
[10:54] Marco Ruiz: Thanks all.
[11:00] End call.

Notes on transcript: occasional filler and overlapping talk; some product names transcribed as "Redwood dedicate" or "dedicate" in places. References to privacy and compliance were prioritized by Priya and Marta.
